title: The Sermon at Benares (poem: For Anne Gregory)

learn.hook: A mother looks for a cure for her sorrow and is asked for something very simple: a few mustard seeds. Why?
points: 'The Sermon at Benares' tells how Gautama Buddha helped Kisa Gotami, a mother grieving for her son.
He asked her to bring mustard seed from a house where no one had ever died. She found no such house and understood that death comes to every family.
The teaching: grief is natural, but endless sorrow brings only more pain; understanding that loss is shared by all can bring peace.
Connectors join ideas: contrast (although, but, however), reason (because, since, as), result (so, therefore), addition (and, moreover).
'However' and 'therefore' usually link two sentences: 'It rained. However, the fair went on.'

example.q: Passage: When Arjun's grandfather passed away, Arjun shut himself in his room. His aunt sat beside him and said gently, 'Every family we know has lost someone. Grief shared is grief halved.' Slowly, Arjun opened the window. What did the aunt mean by 'Grief shared is grief halved'?
steps: She reminds Arjun that every family has lost someone.
So he is not alone in his sorrow.
Talking about it with others makes the pain lighter, just as Kisa Gotami found that loss is common to all.
example.answer: Sharing sorrow with others makes it easier to bear.

learn.reallife: Families across India come together after a loss to support each other; comfort from others helps people heal.

quiz.q: Whose teaching is described in 'The Sermon at Benares'?
quiz.explain: The lesson is about the Buddha and Kisa Gotami.
quiz.mistake: Confuses different great teachers of India

quiz.q: What did the Buddha ask Kisa Gotami to bring?
options: Mustard seed from a house where no one had died
A lamp lit in every house
quiz.explain: He asked for mustard seed from a house that had never known death.

quiz.q: What did Kisa Gotami finally understand?
quiz.explain: No house was free of death, so she saw that loss is common to all.
quiz.mistake: Focuses on the seed rather than the lesson

quiz.q: Passage: When Arjun's grandfather passed away, Arjun shut himself in his room. His aunt sat beside him and said gently, 'Every family we know has lost someone. Grief shared is grief halved.' Slowly, Arjun opened the window. What did the aunt's words mean?
options: Grief can be cut into two pieces
Arjun should stay in his room
Only half the family was sad
Sharing sorrow makes it easier to bear
quiz.explain: 'Grief shared is grief halved' means sorrow feels lighter when shared.

quiz.q: Choose the connector: 'Arjun was sad. ___, he went to school.'
quiz.explain: Going to school despite being sad shows contrast: 'However'.
quiz.mistake: Uses a connector of reason or result

quiz.q: Choose the connector: 'She could not find the seed ___ every house had lost someone.'
quiz.explain: The second part gives the reason, so 'because' fits.
quiz.mistake: Uses a contrast word where a reason is needed

quiz.q: Choose the connector: '___ it was raining, they went to the fair.'
quiz.explain: Going despite rain is a contrast: 'Although'.
quiz.mistake: Misses the unexpected link between rain and going out

quiz.explain: To console is to comfort in grief or disappointment.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of the noun 'console' (a gaming device)

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend's pet fish died and she won't stop crying. What can I tell her, like the Buddha told Kisa Gotami?
teach.praise: Soft chirp... I'll comfort her and remind her that loss comes to everyone, and sharing makes it lighter.
teach.nudge: What did Kisa Gotami learn about who faces loss? How can sharing help?

topics.title: Inner vs outer beauty: opposites with prefixes

learn.hook: Would you rather be liked for your hair or for your heart?
points: 'For Anne Gregory' is by the Irish poet W.B. Yeats. A young woman wants to be loved for herself, not for her beautiful yellow hair.
The older speaker replies that people are usually attracted first by outer looks; the poem contrasts outer beauty with inner worth.
Inner beauty: kindness, honesty, courage. Outer beauty: looks, hair, clothes.
Many opposites are formed with prefixes: un- (unkind), in- (invisible), im- before p/m (impossible, immature), il- before l (illegal), ir- before r (irregular), dis- (dishonest).
Superficial means 'only on the surface', which is the opposite of looking at inner qualities.

example.q: Poem: 'Don't praise my curls,' my sister said, / 'Praise the kindness that I do.' / Dadi laughed, 'Child, most eyes will see / Your curls before they look at you.' What does the sister want, and what does Dadi say about the world?
steps: The sister wants her kindness praised, not her curls: inner beauty.
Dadi says most people notice curls (outer beauty) first.
So the poem contrasts inner and outer beauty.
example.answer: The sister wants to be valued for her kindness; Dadi says people usually notice looks first.

learn.reallife: Long after school photos fade, friends remember who was kind, honest and helpful. Character outlasts looks.

games.title: Beauty and the poem
items: 'For Anne Gregory' was written by W.B. Yeats.
The young woman wants to be loved for her yellow hair.
She wants to be loved for herself, not her hair.
Kindness is an example of inner beauty.
It is 'illegal'; il- is used before words starting with l.
Superficial judgement looks only at the outside.

quiz.explain: The poem is by the Irish poet W.B. Yeats.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up poets of First Flight

quiz.q: What does the young woman in 'For Anne Gregory' want?
options: To dye her hair a new colour
To be loved for herself, not for her yellow hair
quiz.explain: She wants to be valued for who she is inside.
quiz.mistake: Thinks she wants more admiration for her looks

quiz.q: What is the main theme of 'For Anne Gregory'?
quiz.explain: The poem contrasts being loved for looks with being loved for oneself.
quiz.mistake: Takes the poem as only describing hair

quiz.q: Poem: 'Don't praise my curls,' my sister said, / 'Praise the kindness that I do.' / Dadi laughed, 'Child, most eyes will see / Your curls before they look at you.' What does the sister want praised?
quiz.explain: She says, 'Praise the kindness that I do.'
quiz.mistake: Picks the outer feature she rejects
Adds the most common prefix 'un-' to every word

quiz.explain: Words starting with r often take ir-: irresponsible.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the ir- rule before r

options: Only on the surface; not deep
quiz.explain: Superficial means concerned only with what is on the outside.

teach.ask: Gappu: Everyone praises my shiny feathers, but I want them to like ME. What is the poem 'For Anne Gregory' saying?
teach.praise: Chirp-chirp! It's about inner beauty versus outer looks. I'll be loved for my kind heart!
teach.nudge: Which matters in the poem: outside looks or what is inside? Can you name both?
